source_refs.note: Exercise 4.2, Question 4: Cofactors and determinants of A and B, parts (i)-(ii) (book page 60).

blocks.explanation:
A cofactor question: \(A_{ij}\) is the cofactor of the entry in row \(i\), column \(j\), not the entry itself.
All three asked cofactors belong to column 3, so afterwards we find \(|A|\) by expanding along column 3.
Plan: cover, find the minor, attach the sign \((-1)^{i+j}\); then \(|A| = a_{13}A_{13} + a_{23}A_{23} + a_{33}A_{33}\).
steps:
Given: \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 \\ -2 & -2 & 7 \end{bmatrix}\)
To find: \(A_{13}, A_{23}, A_{33}\) and \(|A|\).
Method: \(A_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j}M_{ij}\), where the minor \(M_{ij}\) is the \(2 \times 2\) determinant left after deleting row \(i\) and column \(j\).

\(|A|\) by expansion along column 3
\[|A| = a_{13}A_{13} + a_{23}A_{23} + a_{33}A_{33}\]
\[= (-3)(-10) + (0)(-2) + (7)(-5)\]
\[= 30 + 0 - 35 = -5\]
Why: A determinant equals the sum of the entries of any column times their own cofactors. The signs are already inside the cofactors.

Check (expand along row 2)
\[|A| = (-5)(+1)\begin{vmatrix} 1 & -3 \\ -2 & 7 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= -5(7 - 6) = -5 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Row 2 is \(0, -5, 0\); only \(a_{22}\) counts, with sign \(+\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: For part (i) the answer key prints \(A_{13} = -3,\ A_{23} = 0,\ A_{33} = 7\). These are the entries \(a_{13}, a_{23}, a_{33}\) of \(A\), not the cofactors. The cofactors are \(A_{13} = -10,\ A_{23} = -2,\ A_{33} = -5\). The key's \(|A| = -5\) is correct.

blocks.explanation:
Again cofactors: \(B_{3j}\) is the cofactor of the entry in row 3, column \(j\).
All three are in row 3, so afterwards we expand \(|B|\) along row 3.
Plan: three cofactors with signs \(+,\,-,\,+\), then \(|B| = b_{31}B_{31} + b_{32}B_{32} + b_{33}B_{33}\).
steps:
Given: \(B = \begin{bmatrix} -5 & -2 & 5 \\ -3 & -1 & 4 \\ -2 & -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\)
To find: \(B_{31}, B_{32}, B_{33}\) and \(|B|\).
Method: \(B_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j}M_{ij}\); then expansion along row 3.

Cofactor \(B_{33}\) (delete row 3, column 3)
\[B_{33} = (-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix} -5 & -2 \\ -3 & -1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= +[(-5)(-1) - (-2)(-3)]\]
\[= 5 - 6 = -1\]
Why: Sign \(+\); both products are positive.

\(|B|\) by expansion along row 3
\[|B| = b_{31}B_{31} + b_{32}B_{32} + b_{33}B_{33}\]
\[= (-2)(-3) + (-1)(5) + (2)(-1)\]
\[= 6 - 5 - 2 = -1\]
Why: Entries of row 3 times their own cofactors.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: For part (ii) the answer key prints \(B_{31} = -2,\ B_{32} = -1,\ B_{33} = 2\). These are the entries \(b_{31}, b_{32}, b_{33}\) of \(B\), not the cofactors. The cofactors are \(B_{31} = -3,\ B_{32} = 5,\ B_{33} = -1\). The key's \(|B| = -1\) is correct.
